questions_and_answers.question: Acids and bases have been defined in different ways. Arrhenius defined an acid as a compound that dissolves in water to increase the concentration of H+, and a base as a compound that increases the concentration of OH−. Later, Brønsted and Lowry modified the definition: Acids are proton donors, and bases are proton acceptors. The Brønsted-Lowry definition of acids and bases is represented generically by this reaction, where HA is an acid and BB is a base: HA+B⇌A−+BH+HA+B⇌A−+BH+ An acid that has lost a proton is that acid's conjugate base (A−). A base that has accepted a proton is that base's conjugate acid (BH+). For each acid-base reaction, there are two conjugate acid-base pairs. The word conjugate is related to the word conjugal, which means "having to do with marriage." A wife is only a wife to her husband, and a husband is only a husband to his wife. Similarly, a conjugate acid is defined as "conjugate" only in relation to the base from which it is derived, and a conjugate base is so defined only in relation to the acid from which it is derived. Conjugate acid-base pairs are identified as pairs because they are defined only in relation to each other. Phosphoric acid reacts with water to yield dihydrogen phosphate ions and hydronium ions: H3PO4+H2O⇌H2PO−4+H3O+ Identify the conjugate acid-base pairs.

questions_and_answers.question: Phosphoric acid reacts with water to yield dihydrogen phosphate ions and hydronium ions: H3PO4+H2O⇌H2PO4−+H3O+ Identify the conjugate acid-base pairs. Drag each item to the appropriate bin phosphoric acid: H3PO4 hydronium ion water: H2O dihydrogen phosphate: H2PO4(-)
questions_and_answers.answer: Conjugate Acid-Base Pairs In an acid-base reaction, the species that donates a proton (H+) is called the acid, while the species that accepts a proton is called the base. After the reaction, the acid becomes its conjugate base (by losing a proton) and the base becomes its conjugate acid (by gaining a proton). In the given reaction: H3PO4 + H2O ⇌ H2PO4(-) + H3O+ We can identify the conjugate acid-base pairs as follows: Phosphoric acid (H3PO4) and Dihydrogen phosphate (H2PO4-) Phosphoric acid (H3PO4) donates a proton to become dihydrogen phosphate (H2PO4-), so H3PO4 is the acid and H2PO4- is its conjugate base. Water (H2O) and Hydronium ion (H3O+) Water (H2O) accepts a proton to become hydronium ion (H3O+), so H2O is the base and H3O+ is its conjugate acid. Here is a table summarizing the conjugate acid-base pairs: Acid Conjugate Base Base Conjugate Acid H3PO4 H2PO4- H2O H3O+
